The ticket

A frozen ticket names its protocol version, baseline digest, source, verifier, benchmark metric and repetitions, correctness rule, acceptance threshold, policy, reward, and deadline. Changing the question creates a new contract.

Inspect the full proposed schema →

The review path

01 / Freeze

The requester commits the exact source, benchmark, verifier, policy, and deadline, then funds the reward.

02 / Build

A builder submits a patch, reproducible build manifest, measurements, and a proof bundle.

03 / Critique

Diverse critics check semantics, performance, security, supply chain, and reproducibility from independent environments.

04 / Challenge

Verdicts are committed before other reports become visible. A replayable counterexample can trigger the challenge policy.

05 / Settle

A quorum of signed attestations settles the ticket. Review fees, failure bounties, bonds, and the builder reward follow its frozen policy.

Proof and economics

Start with deterministic replay and independent critics. Selective cryptographic proof bundles may establish a specified computation later; they do not define what an ambiguous benchmark means.

The delivery plan begins with a local escrow-backed proof loop. A token is optional future infrastructure. The product does not need a coin to determine whether an acceptance command passed.
